Terrestrial Cool Flame Experiments

Counterflow Diffusion Flame





            Cool diffusion flame, 1 g (Won et al.)
                                           Excellent configuration for studying flame’s strength under the
                                                           effect of stretch.
                                       Useful platform for validating reaction kinetics and transport
                                                models.
                                           Idealized condition, it can be treated as a 1D problem:

                                     Leads to the derivation of an analytical solution
                                   Makes numerical modeling tractable

Limitations of the conventional numerical approach

    The numerical effort to study counterflow flame configuration has been predominantly centered
       upon OPPDIF module of CHEMKIN chemical kinetic package
    This module implements a similarity transformation approach that reduces the flow field to a
         one-dimensional/ plug flow problem with the following assumptions:

       Radial component of velocity is linear in radius
       Dependent variables become functions of the axial direction only



               What are the physical conditions that can be
                         represented by this assumption?


                                                             Cool flames

 High Reynolds number flow configuration: High strain rate (a)
 Thin flame sheet: Hot flame (high activation energy)           Low Re: Low strain rate (a ~100 s-1)
                                                           Finite Flame Thickness: low activation energy)

Effect of buoyancy

                                                          Buoyancy lifts the flame
                                                                          upward.

                                                              Without buoyancy, 1D and
                                                           2D models predict the flame
                                                                                          at or near the stagnation
                                                                             plane due to momentum-
                                                                          balanced BC.
a) Temperature distribution and streamlines, and b) heat release rate, for DME diffusion cool flame
with and without buoyancy for identical conditions (XDME= 0.587, UF = 62.3 cm/s, UO = 50.9 cm/s, a ~
90 s-1, P = 1 atm)                                        The peak flame temperature
                                                                                                in 1D is slightly lower
                                                                   compared to the 2D
                                                                                         prediction, but the peak HRR
                                                                   shows the opposite trend.

                                                               Temperature gradient is
                                                                                 higher in 1D calculation.
                                                                  More diffusive heat loss.

Flow field analyses


                                            The extended entrance channels
                                                                           allow the velocity at the nozzle exits
                                                                                  to be perturbed by the flame.

                                       2D model captures the perturbation
                                                                                        in a self-consistent manner.

                                       2D model without buoyancy retains
                                                                          the momentum-balanced condition
                       c                        d          and forms the stagnation plane at the
                                                                             axis midpoint, exhibiting identical
                                                                             perturbation on either side

                                                                   observed in experiments of Sarnecki
                                                                                  et al.

Summary

    • Insights obtained from modeling on cool flame characteristics and
    dynamics

    • Models were developed for a number of scenarios

    • Models were validated against the FLEX data and then utilized to
     explore other scenarios

    • Extensive amount of experimental data available for interpretation
    and new insights

pages.text:
Limitations of the conventional numerical approach

    The numerical effort to study counterflow flame configuration has been predominantly centered
       upon OPPDIF module of CHEMKIN chemical kinetic package
    This module implements a similarity transformation approach that reduces the flow field to a
         one-dimensional/ plug flow problem with the following assumptions:

       Radial component of velocity is linear in radius
       Dependent variables become functions of the axial direction only



               What are the physical conditions that can be
                         represented by this assumption?


                                                             Cool flames

 High Reynolds number flow configuration: High strain rate (a)
 Thin flame sheet: Hot flame (high activation energy)           Low Re: Low strain rate (a ~100 s-1)
                                                           Finite Flame Thickness: low activation energy)

Summary

    • Insights obtained from modeling on cool flame characteristics and
    dynamics

    • Models were developed for a number of scenarios

    • Models were validated against the FLEX data and then utilized to
     explore other scenarios

    • Extensive amount of experimental data available for interpretation
    and new insights
